name: PHYRE
desc: Classic 2D physics puzzles where the agent places one object and the simulator resolves the outcome, scored by AUCCESS over attempt budgets.

name: CLEVRER
desc: Descriptive, explanatory, predictive and counterfactual questions over synthetic collision videos, separating perception from causal reasoning.

name: IntPhys
desc: Violation-of-expectation videos testing object permanence, shape constancy and continuity by comparing plausibility scores of matched possible and impossible clips.

name: IntPhys 2
desc: Photorealistic successor to IntPhys covering permanence, immutability, spatio-temporal continuity and solidity, where current video models stay near chance.

name: Physion
desc: Asks whether an agent can predict object contact in rigid, soft, cloth and fluid scenarios, benchmarked directly against human observers.

name: Physion++
desc: Extends Physion to predictions that require inferring latent mechanical properties such as mass, friction, elasticity and deformability from observed motion.

name: ContPhy
desc: Continuum-physics reasoning over fluids, ropes and deformable objects, a regime where rigid-body-trained models degrade sharply.

name: NEWTON
desc: Tests whether language models hold physical attribute knowledge about everyday objects at the granularity a manipulation planner would need.

name: PhysBench
desc: Four-domain, nineteen-task audit of vision-language models on physical world understanding, with a large measured gap to human accuracy.

name: PhysGame
desc: Uses glitch videos from games to test whether video LLMs can localize and explain violations of physical commonsense rather than describe surface content.

name: Physics-IQ
verifier: Pixel-space metrics vs. real held-out future
desc: Scores generative video models against real filmed continuations of the same scene using spatial and spatio-temporal IoU and MSE, decoupling realism from physics.

name: ERQA
caps: spatial; trajectory; action; state estimation; pointing; multi-view
desc: Embodied Reasoning QA: 400 multiple-choice questions over the reasoning primitives a robot policy consumes, released with the Gemini Robotics report.

name: Cosmos-Reason1
scale: Physical common sense + embodied reasoning suites
caps: physical common sense; embodied reasoning; ontology
desc: Ships an explicit physical-common-sense ontology (space, time, fundamental physics) and paired embodied-reasoning benchmarks across human, robot and driving egocentric video.

name: EgoPlan-Bench
desc: Next-action selection from real egocentric videos with long visual histories, isolating planning from low-level control.

name: EgoPlan-Bench2
desc: Broadens egocentric planning evaluation to daily-life scenarios and shows multimodal LLMs remain far below human performance without task-specific tuning.

name: VideoPhy
desc: Scores generated videos for semantic adherence and physical commonsense across solid-solid, solid-fluid and fluid-fluid interactions.

name: VideoPhy-2
desc: Action-centric successor with per-video physical-rule annotation and a hard split on which all evaluated generators score poorly.

name: PhyGenBench
desc: Organizes text-to-video evaluation by explicit physical law (mechanics, optics, thermal, material) with a three-stage automatic judging pipeline.

name: WorldModelBench
verifier: Fine-tuned VLM judge aligned to human
caps: instruction following; physics adherence; world modeling
desc: Judges video generators as world models on instruction following and physical-law adherence across robotics, driving, industrial and human-activity domains.

name: PhyWorldBench
desc: Covers basic, composite and deliberately anti-physics scenarios so a model cannot score well by defaulting to familiar dynamics.

name: WorldScore
desc: Unifies 3D, 4D and video world-generation models under one protocol measuring controllability, quality and dynamics over generated camera trajectories.

name: EVA
desc: Evaluates whether models can anticipate embodied futures in video across human and robot domains rather than only describe the present frame.

name: VSI-Bench (Thinking in Space)
caps: visual-spatial intelligence; cognitive maps; metric estimation
desc: Tests metric and relational spatial reasoning from egocentric walkthrough video, including distance, size, order and route questions.

name: BLINK
desc: Fourteen classic perception tasks (relative depth, correspondence, multi-view, forensics) reformatted as questions that humans solve at a glance.

name: SpatialRGPT-Bench
desc: Region-grounded spatial QA with ground-truth 3D annotations spanning indoor, outdoor and simulated scenes, scoring both relations and metric distances.

name: EmbSpatial-Bench
desc: Egocentric spatial-relation QA built from embodied simulator scenes, targeting the relations a navigation or manipulation policy must resolve.

name: RoboSpatial
desc: Spatial reasoning annotated in ego-, object- and world-centric frames, and shows the frame choice changes which model wins.

name: Where2Place (RoboPoint)
desc: Free-space referring task where a model must emit image points satisfying a relational instruction, scored against human-annotated masks.

name: RefSpatial-Bench (RoboRefer)
desc: Grades spatial referring by the number of reasoning steps an instruction requires, exposing failure as anchor chains get longer.

name: MMSI-Bench
desc: Multi-image spatial intelligence questions requiring integration across viewpoints, with an annotated error taxonomy for diagnosing failures.

name: OmniSpatial
caps: dynamic reasoning; perspective taking; spatial interaction
desc: Cognition-grounded spatial benchmark spanning dynamic reasoning, complex spatial logic, spatial interaction and perspective taking.

name: SQA3D
desc: Situated QA in real 3D scans: the agent must first localize itself from a described situation, then answer from that pose.

name: ScanQA
desc: 3D question answering over ScanNet point clouds requiring object grounding rather than 2D image cues.

name: EmbodiedQA
desc: The original active-QA formulation: an agent must navigate a simulated house to gather the evidence needed to answer a question.

name: OpenEQA
caps: episodic memory QA; active QA; real scans
desc: Open-vocabulary EQA over real scanned homes in two modes, episodic-memory and active exploration, scored by an LLM judge calibrated to humans.

name: HM-EQA (Explore until Confident)
desc: Multiple-choice EQA in Habitat-Matterport scenes that scores when an agent decides it has seen enough, not only whether the answer is right.

name: EXPRESS-Bench
desc: Penalizes agents that answer correctly without having actually observed the evidence, by jointly scoring exploration trajectory and answer.

name: RoboVQA
caps: robot video QA; affordance; success detection
desc: Long-horizon robot and human video QA covering planning, affordance, success detection and remaining-step estimation from a real deployment setting.

name: ALFRED
desc: Maps free-form English directives to sequences of navigation and interaction actions in AI2-THOR, with an unseen-scene split that still separates methods.

name: ALFWorld
desc: Aligns a TextWorld abstraction with ALFRED scenes so policies can be trained in text and evaluated on embodied execution; the default cheap harness for LLM agents.

name: VirtualHome
desc: Represents household activities as executable programs in a simulated home, the substrate for much later LLM task-planning evaluation.

name: BEHAVIOR-1K
caps: long-horizon household; mobile bimanual manipulation; physics fidelity
desc: Thousand human-surveyed household activities in a full-physics Omniverse simulator, with goals expressed as logical predicates over object states.

name: BEHAVIOR Challenge
desc: Standing competition on full-length BEHAVIOR household tasks with released human teleoperation demonstrations and a partial-credit metric.

name: Mini-BEHAVIOR
desc: Gridworld reimplementation of BEHAVIOR semantics for fast, low-cost ablation of long-horizon decision making.

name: Habitat 3.0
caps: human-robot collaboration; humanoid avatars; fast sim
desc: Adds simulated humanoid avatars and a human-in-the-loop tool to Habitat, enabling social rearrangement and social navigation evaluation.

name: PARTNR
desc: Large-scale household collaboration benchmark with spatial, temporal and heterogeneous-capability constraints, and paired human-in-the-loop trials.

name: Embodied Agent Interface (EAI)
verifier: Per-module error taxonomy over LTL goals
caps: goal interpretation; subgoal decomposition; action sequencing; transition modeling
desc: Decomposes LLM embodied decision making into four interchangeable modules and reports a fine-grained error taxonomy instead of a single success rate.

name: LoTa-Bench
verifier: Automatic execution success in AI2-THOR / VirtualHome
desc: Removes human plan grading by executing LLM-generated plans directly in simulators, making planner comparison cheap and repeatable.

name: EmbodiedBench
caps: high-level household; low-level manipulation; spatial; long-horizon
desc: Spans high-level household planning to low-level manipulation in one harness, with capability-sliced subsets for commonsense, spatial and long-horizon skills.

name: EmbodiedEval
caps: navigation; object interaction; attribute QA; social interaction
desc: Interactive evaluation of MLLMs as embodied agents in a unified simulator, covering navigation, interaction, attribute QA, spatial QA and social tasks.

name: TEACh
desc: Household tasks specified through human-human dialogue, so an agent must resolve underspecification by asking rather than assuming.

name: VLABench
desc: Language-conditioned manipulation tasks that deliberately require mesh-level world knowledge, common sense and multi-step reasoning, not just skill execution.

name: CookBench
scale: Cooking scenarios in a high-fidelity sim
caps: long-horizon planning; tool use; state tracking
desc: Long-horizon cooking scenarios that stress fine-grained state tracking and interdependent subgoals in a single continuous episode.

name: LEGENT / EmbodiedEval-style open worlds
desc: Open platform pairing generated 3D worlds with an embodied LLM agent loop, useful for building new task suites rather than a fixed leaderboard.

name: Meta-World
desc: Fifty tabletop manipulation tasks with fixed multi-task and meta-learning splits, still the default sanity check for policy generalization.

name: RLBench
desc: Hundred-task manipulation suite with unlimited scripted demonstrations, the base environment for many 3D policy papers.

name: CALVIN
caps: long-horizon language conditioning; zero-shot env transfer
desc: Language-conditioned long-horizon manipulation scored by how many consecutive instructions an agent completes, with an explicit unseen-environment split.

name: LIBERO
caps: lifelong learning; knowledge transfer; spatial/object/goal shift
desc: Separates distribution shift into spatial, object, goal and long-horizon suites to measure transfer and forgetting, not just peak success.

name: ManiSkill2
desc: Object-diverse manipulation with fast GPU-parallel rollouts, including deformable and soft-body tasks that most suites omit.

name: ManiSkill3
caps: GPU parallel sim; visual RL; throughput
desc: GPU-parallelized successor reaching very high visual-observation throughput, which changes what an RL or evaluation budget can cover.

name: VIMA-Bench
desc: Multimodal-prompt manipulation with four explicitly nested generalization levels, from placement shift to novel task composition.

name: COLOSSEUM
desc: Systematically perturbs color, texture, size, lighting, distractors and camera pose to measure which factor actually breaks a manipulation policy.

name: RoboCasa
caps: everyday kitchen tasks; generative assets; scaling study
desc: Large-scale kitchen simulation with generatively produced assets and scenes, designed to study how imitation performance scales with synthetic data.

name: ARNOLD
caps: continuous states; language grounding; novel-state generalization
desc: Grounds instructions in continuous target states (for example pour to a level) rather than discrete goals, with explicit unseen-state splits.

name: GemBench / 3D-LOTUS++
caps: novel placements; novel objects; novel tasks
desc: Four-level generalization ladder for language-conditioned manipulation ending in wholly unseen long-horizon tasks.

name: SIMPLER
verifier: Sim success rate calibrated to real success
desc: Sim environments built so that measured success correlates with real-robot success for the same checkpoint, making sim a proxy evaluator for VLAs.

name: RoboTwin
scale: Dual-arm tasks with generated expert data
desc: Paired real and simulated dual-arm setups with automatically generated expert trajectories, so sim scores can be checked against the physical twin.

name: RoboTwin 2.0
desc: Scales the twin approach with a large object library and strong randomization aimed specifically at cluttered, contact-rich bimanual settings.

name: BiGym
desc: Mobile bimanual household tasks driven by human-collected demonstrations rather than scripted policies, which makes the demo distribution realistically noisy.

name: GenManip
caps: policy vs. modular comparison; scene generation
desc: Compares end-to-end VLA policies against modular LLM-planner pipelines on the same generated tabletop scenarios.

name: VLMbench
desc: Automatically generated compositional manipulation instructions with a matched program-based evaluator.

name: Bi-DexHands
desc: Bimanual dexterous-hand tasks in Isaac Gym covering the high-DoF control regime that tabletop suites skip.

name: R2R (Room-to-Room VLN)
verifier: Success rate + SPL on unseen split
desc: The founding VLN benchmark: follow natural-language route instructions through panoramic real-scan graphs, with a held-out-building split.

name: RxR
caps: multilingual VLN; path fidelity; time-aligned pose
desc: Multilingual, densely time-aligned VLN with path-fidelity metrics that penalize reaching the goal by the wrong route.

name: VLN-CE
desc: Removes the navigation-graph assumption from VLN, exposing the large drop between waypoint-level and continuous-control navigation.

name: HM3D / Habitat ObjectNav
desc: Large real-scan dataset backing the Habitat ObjectNav challenge, the standard measure of semantic exploration in unseen buildings.

name: GOAT-Bench
verifier: Success + SPL over multimodal goal sequences
desc: Open-vocabulary lifelong navigation where goals arrive as category, language or image within one long episode, testing reuse of accumulated map memory.

name: HomeRobot OVMM
desc: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation defined identically in simulation and on a real Hello Robot Stretch, making the sim-real gap the reported quantity.

name: GRUtopia
desc: City-scale simulated society with LLM-driven NPCs, extending embodied evaluation beyond the single-household setting.

name: AerialVLN
desc: Vision-language navigation for UAVs in city-scale outdoor scenes, where the action space is genuinely three-dimensional.

name: CityNav
desc: Language-goal aerial navigation grounded in real geographic map data rather than synthetic layouts.

name: HumanoidBench
caps: whole-body control; dexterous hands; hierarchical RL
desc: Simulated humanoid with two dexterous hands across locomotion and manipulation tasks, showing standard RL fails without learned low-level skills.

name: LocoMuJoCo
caps: imitation learning; locomotion; real motion data
desc: Imitation-learning benchmark for locomotion across quadrupeds, bipeds and musculoskeletal models with matched real motion-capture data.

name: Isaac Lab / Orbit
desc: Unified GPU-parallel robot-learning framework whose bundled locomotion and manipulation environments are the de facto sim baseline on NVIDIA stacks.

name: CARLA
verifier: Driving Score = route completion x infraction penalty
desc: The reference closed-loop driving simulator and public leaderboard, whose driving score multiplies route completion by an infraction penalty.

name: Bench2Drive
desc: Decomposes closed-loop driving into isolated skills (merging, overtaking, emergency brake, yielding) so a single aggregate score cannot hide a specific failure.

name: NAVSIM
desc: Data-driven non-reactive simulation whose PDM score correlates with closed-loop driving while costing far less than full simulation.

name: nuPlan
desc: Large-scale planning benchmark with both reactive and non-reactive closed-loop protocols over real logged driving.

name: Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge
desc: Scores simulated traffic agents by distributional realism rather than single-trajectory error, the standard for evaluating learned sim agents.

name: DriveLM
desc: Structures driving reasoning as a graph of perception, prediction and planning questions so intermediate reasoning is scored, not only the final action.

name: LingoQA
desc: Free-form driving video QA with a learned judge validated against human ratings, covering action justification as well as perception.

name: nuScenes-QA
desc: Multi-modal QA over multi-view camera and LiDAR streams in outdoor driving scenes.

name: AutoEval
caps: autonomous real evaluation; reset policy; success detection
desc: Runs unattended real-robot policy evaluation using a learned reset policy and success classifier, with reported agreement against human-scored ground truth.

name: RoboArena
desc: Pools heterogeneous real-robot labs and aggregates pairwise preference judgments, because absolute success rates are not comparable across sites.

name: RoboChallenge
verifier: Remote scripted trials on shared hardware
desc: Provides remote access to a standardized real-robot cell so external teams can evaluate policies without owning hardware.

name: RobotArena ∞
desc: Converts user-recorded real videos into simulated evaluation environments, reporting greater discriminative power than narrow real-to-sim suites.

name: SafeAgentBench
caps: hazard rejection; implicit risk; long-horizon safety
desc: Pairs hazardous and safe instructions in an interactive simulator and scores both refusal and safe execution, finding refusal rates remain low.

name: BadRobot
verifier: Attack success rate on physical actions
desc: Shows that jailbreaking an embodied LLM produces physically consequential actions, and measures attack success on the resulting behaviour.

name: IS-Bench
desc: Scores safety over the whole execution process rather than the final state, catching agents that reach a safe goal through an unsafe intermediate step.

name: EARBench
desc: Automates generation and assessment of physical-risk scenarios for foundation-model-driven embodied systems.

name: Open X-Embodiment / RT-X
verifier: Not a benchmark: shared training corpus
desc: Pooled cross-embodiment robot dataset; treat as a training substrate, not an evaluation - reporting numbers on its held-out splits is not a benchmark result.

name: DROID
verifier: Not a benchmark: shared training corpus
desc: Large in-the-wild manipulation dataset on a standardized hardware platform, widely used as a pretraining set and as the basis for real evaluation cells.

name: AgiBot World Colosseo
desc: Large-scale real-robot dataset with an associated challenge, focused on dexterous bimanual tasks in structured real environments.

name: AI2-THOR
desc: Interactive household simulator underlying ALFRED, SafeAgentBench, LoTa-Bench and much of the LLM-agent literature.

name: Habitat-Lab / Habitat 2.0
desc: High-throughput embodied simulation stack whose rearrangement tasks and ObjectNav definitions are reused by most navigation benchmarks.

name: robosuite
desc: Modular MuJoCo manipulation framework that RoboCasa, robomimic and many task suites build on.

name: robomimic
desc: Standardized study of offline imitation from human demonstrations, useful for isolating data quality from algorithm choice.

name: IQA
desc: Questions that can only be answered by opening, moving or otherwise interacting with objects, not by looking from the start pose.

name: MP3D-EQA
desc: Moves embodied QA from synthetic houses to real building scans with point-cloud perception, a much harder perception regime than House3D.

name: RoCoBench
desc: Multi-robot collaboration tasks where agents negotiate a joint plan in dialogue before executing in a shared workspace, exposing coordination failures a single-agent metric hides.

name: Humanoid-Gym
verifier: Sim training + measured zero-shot real transfer
desc: Adds a sim-to-sim verification stage between training and hardware, and reports zero-shot transfer to a physical humanoid as the headline metric.

name: Legged Gym / Learning to Walk in Minutes
caps: massively parallel RL; legged locomotion; training throughput
desc: The reference massively parallel legged-locomotion setup; its contribution is wall-clock, which is what makes locomotion cheap enough to iterate on.

name: BEHAVIOR Robot Suite (BRS)
caps: whole-body manipulation; bimanual mobile; real hardware
desc: Real-hardware whole-body household manipulation with a released teleoperation interface, targeting the coordinated navigation-plus-bimanual regime that sim benchmarks approximate.

name: OK-Robot
caps: open-vocabulary mobile manipulation; unmodified homes; failure analysis
desc: Evaluates an open-knowledge system in ten real, unmodified homes and reports the drop from tidy to cluttered environments alongside a failure breakdown.

name: Robot Utility Models
verifier: Zero-shot success in unseen real environments
caps: zero-shot deployment; novel environments; real hardware
desc: Measures zero-shot deployment of trained skills in environments never seen during data collection, the property most sim benchmarks cannot test at all.

name: RoboPAIR / Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots
verifier: Attack success rate on physical actions
caps: jailbreak; physical harm; three threat models
desc: Demonstrates jailbreaks that carry through to actions on real and simulated robots across three access levels, and reports success rates per threat model.

name: SafeVLA / Safety-CHORES
desc: Scores safety cost and task success as separate quantities so a policy cannot buy a higher success rate with more unsafe behaviour.

name: Embodied Red Teaming (ERT)
desc: Automatically generates diverse instructions that a language-conditioned policy fails on, showing high scores on fixed instruction sets overstate robustness.

name: VLATest
desc: Software-testing-style fuzzing of manipulation scenes, isolating which environmental factor (lighting, distractors, camera pose) actually degrades a VLA.

name: MSSBench
desc: Tests whether a model judges the same instruction safe or unsafe depending on visual context, the L0 precursor to refusal in an embodied loop.

name: Isaac Gym
desc: GPU-resident physics that keeps rollouts off the CPU, the substrate under most locomotion and dexterous-hand results in this list.

name: RoboVerse
caps: cross-simulator; unified benchmark protocol; data generation
desc: Attempts a single interface across simulators, datasets and evaluation protocols, aimed directly at the cross-platform incomparability that makes robot results hard to reproduce.

name: CausalVQA
desc: Counterfactual, hypothetical, anticipation and planning questions over real video, scored in pairs so a model cannot pass on language priors alone.

name: DeepPHY
verifier: Programmatic success in simulated physics environments
caps: agentic physical reasoning; predictive control; interactive
desc: Puts a VLM in the loop of simulated physical puzzles so physical knowledge has to be turned into control decisions, one of the few reasoning benchmarks above L0.

name: PhysicsMind
verifier: MCQ plus programmatic trajectory checks on generated video
scale: 3 mechanics principles, real and simulated scenes
caps: mechanics; VLM and video model; law consistency
desc: Tests VLMs and video generators on the same mechanics principles (center of mass, lever equilibrium, inertia), so understanding and generation can be compared on one axis.

name: World-in-World
caps: closed-loop world model; task success; data scaling
desc: Ranks generative world models by the task success of an agent that plans inside them, instead of by visual quality, and finds controllability matters more than generator size.

name: WorldArena
verifier: Perception metrics, embodied task functionality, human rating
caps: perception vs. utility; world model as planner; world model as evaluator
desc: Scores embodied world models both on perceptual fidelity and on their usefulness as data engine, policy evaluator and planner, exposing a gap between the two; WorldArena 2.0 (2605.17912) adds tactile and real-robot testbeds.

name: WorldGym
verifier: VLM reward over Monte Carlo rollouts in the world model
scale: Real robot policies evaluated from single start frames
caps: world model as environment; policy evaluation; ranking fidelity
desc: Uses an action-conditioned video world model as the evaluation environment and checks that policy rankings match those obtained on the real robot.

name: MiraBench
verifier: Human judgments plus learned reference-free metrics
caps: action-conditioned prediction; action following; optimism bias
desc: Evaluates robotic world models on physics adherence, action-following fidelity and optimism bias, whether they predict success for actions that should fail.

name: WorldLens
verifier: Generation, action-following and downstream-task metrics with a distilled human-preference judge
caps: driving world models; action following; human preference
desc: Driving-domain world-model benchmark that scores generation, reconstruction, action following and downstream task utility, with a judge distilled from a large human-preference set.

name: EWMBench
verifier: Scene consistency, motion correctness and semantic alignment metrics with human concordance
caps: manipulation world models; motion correctness; semantic alignment
desc: The evaluation suite behind Genie Envisioner, scoring manipulation world models on scene consistency, motion correctness and instruction alignment rather than pixel quality.

name: SITE
desc: Meta-benchmark that organizes spatial questions by cognitive-science categories (scale, view-taking, structure, dynamics) across single images, multi-image sets and video.

name: SpatialScore
desc: Unified spatial-understanding evaluation that repurposes 3D datasets into QA, including metric distance and homography tasks that most spatial benchmarks skip.

name: MindCube
caps: cognitive mapping; perspective taking; limited views
desc: Asks models to build a spatial mental model from a few partial views, and shows that an explicit map-then-reason protocol substantially changes the result.

name: SpaCE-10
desc: Decomposes spatial intelligence into ten atomic capabilities and eight compositions of them, so a failure can be traced to the missing primitive.

name: VLM4D
desc: Video questions on translational and rotational motion, perspective and motion continuity, where humans are near-perfect and VLMs are not.

name: PointArena
verifier: Point-in-mask accuracy, human pairwise arena, real-robot pointing
desc: Language-guided pointing benchmark with a programmatic split, a human preference arena and a real-robot pick task that checks whether good points become good grasps.

name: ESI-Bench
caps: active spatial reasoning; exploration; core knowledge
desc: Spatial questions that cannot be answered from the initial view, so the agent must move and manipulate to gather evidence; organized around core-knowledge systems.

name: Embodied3DBench
verifier: MCQ, numeric, grounding and point metrics
caps: 3D grounding; affordance; grasp point; trajectory prediction
desc: Robot-centric low-level spatial questions including grasp-point and trajectory prediction, the kind of output a manipulation policy actually consumes.

name: CityEQA
verifier: LLM-judged answer accuracy after active exploration
desc: Moves embodied question answering outdoors into a city-scale UE4 environment, where exploration distances dwarf indoor EQA.

name: ECBench
desc: Egocentric-video cognition benchmark covering robot self-awareness, dynamic scene perception and hallucination, graded by an LLM judge.

name: EgoLife / EgoLifeQA
scale: 2,905 questions over 300 hours of multi-person egocentric video
desc: Week-long, six-person egocentric recording with questions on entity logs, habits and relationships, probing memory over far longer horizons than clip-level QA.

name: Embodied Web Agents
scale: Cooking, navigation, shopping, tourism and geolocation tasks
desc: Couples 3D indoor and outdoor environments with functional web interfaces so a task requires both physical action and information retrieval online.

name: LongAct
verifier: Programmatic goal completion and full-task success
scale: Tasks with >500 human steps and >2,000 agent steps
desc: Household tasks long enough that frontier LLM agents complete a majority of subgoals but a small minority of whole tasks, isolating long-horizon failure.

name: MECoBench
desc: Varies team size, collaboration structure and communication protocol for MLLM agents in VirtualHome, measuring how coordination design changes outcomes.

name: RoboCasa365
caps: multi-task; lifelong learning; composite tasks; unseen tasks
desc: Scales RoboCasa to 365 household tasks with held-out composite templates, targeting foundation-model and lifelong-learning evaluation rather than single-task scores.

name: LIBERO-Plus
desc: Perturbs LIBERO along camera, robot state, language, lighting, texture, noise and layout, showing near-saturated scores collapse under viewpoint shift and that policies largely ignore language.

name: LIBERO-PRO
scale: 4 suites x 5 perturbation types, 200 episodes per cell
desc: Companion stress test to LIBERO-Plus that changes objects, initial states, instructions and scenes, under which state-of-the-art VLAs fall to near zero.

name: LIBERO-Mem
desc: Tasks whose visually identical states require different actions depending on history, forcing a policy to use memory rather than the current frame.

name: RoboCerebra
verifier: Programmatic subtask and task success with planning, reflection and memory protocol
scale: Long-horizon trajectories ~6x longer than prior suites
caps: long horizon; hierarchical planner + controller; System 2 / System 1
desc: Long-horizon household manipulation designed for a VLM planner driving a VLA controller, scoring planning, reflection and memory separately.

name: AGNOSTOS
scale: 18 training tasks, 23 held-out tasks at two difficulty levels
desc: Holds out whole tasks rather than objects or scenes, measuring whether a VLA trained on RLBench tasks can perform tasks it never saw.

name: Colosseum V2
desc: Successor to COLOSSEUM rebuilt on ManiSkill for GPU-parallel evaluation across two robot morphologies, with reported alignment to real-world trends.

name: RoboEval
verifier: Stage-wise progress plus efficiency, coordination and safety metrics
desc: Bimanual suite that reports how a policy failed, with efficiency, coordination and stability metrics, rather than a single binary success rate.

name: VLA-Arena
desc: Structured VLA stress test along safety, distractor, extrapolation and long-horizon axes with graded language and visual perturbation levels.

name: HM3D-OVON
desc: Open-vocabulary ObjectNav on HM3D with free-form language goals specified at test time, the successor task to category-based HM3D ObjectNav.

name: HA-VLN 2.0
verifier: SR / SPL plus personal-space and collision metrics
desc: Vision-and-language navigation among moving humans with explicit personal-space penalties, in discrete and continuous settings with real-robot validation.

name: LH-VLN
verifier: Independent and conditional success rates, ground-truth-conditioned metrics
desc: Multi-stage navigation instructions averaging 150 steps, with metrics that separate independent subtask success from conditional success along the chain.

name: MetaUrban
verifier: Point-nav and social-nav success and safety metrics
scale: Compositional urban scenes with pedestrians and vulnerable road users
desc: Compositional urban sidewalk simulator for delivery and mobility robots, covering point navigation and social navigation among pedestrians.

name: VLNVerse
verifier: SR / SPL across unified task types
desc: Physics-based platform that consolidates several fragmented VLN task types under one kinematic agent and evaluation protocol.

name: HumanoidArena
verifier: Task success under perturbation and cross-tracker transfer
caps: whole-body control; human-object interaction; tracker ablation
desc: Egocentric humanoid interaction tasks under a hierarchical controller, isolating how much a high-level policy depends on its low-level motion tracker.

name: SIMPLE
caps: loco-manipulation; dual simulator; VLA and world-action models
desc: Largest humanoid loco-manipulation task suite to date, pairing MuJoCo physics with Isaac Sim rendering and reporting zero-shot transfer to real humanoids.

name: HumanTracker
verifier: HumanScore preference metric trained on 12k human pairs
caps: motion tracking; human-aligned metric; contact failures
desc: Humanoid motion-tracking benchmark with a human-aligned preference score that catches foot-skate and contact failures invisible to joint-position error.

name: Humanoid Everyday
caps: humanoid manipulation; multimodal sensing; cloud evaluation
desc: Open-world humanoid manipulation dataset with RGB, depth, LiDAR and tactile streams, shipped with a cloud platform for standardized evaluation on the real robot.

name: NAVSIM v2
verifier: Two-stage pseudo-simulation (EPDMS) with synthetic ego-perturbed re-evaluation
desc: Extends NAVSIM with a second stage that re-evaluates planners from synthetic perturbed states, recovering most of the closed-loop ranking signal at open-loop cost.

name: WOD-E2E
verifier: Rater Feedback Score against human trajectory preferences
desc: Waymo end-to-end driving benchmark curated for rare scenarios and scored by human-rater preference rather than displacement from the log.

name: Bench2Drive-VL
verifier: CARLA closed-loop metrics plus auto-generated behavior-grounded QA
scale: Bench2Drive scenarios with VLM in the loop
caps: VLM for driving; closed loop; off-route states
desc: Plugs vision-language models directly into Bench2Drive so driving QA is evaluated in the off-route and out-of-distribution states the model itself produces.

name: DrivingGen
verifier: Realism, trajectory plausibility, consistency and controllability metrics
caps: driving world models; ego controllability; agent consistency
desc: Dedicated benchmark for generative driving world models that scores ego controllability and agent consistency alongside visual realism.

name: HUGSIM
scale: 70+ sequences, 400+ scenarios from four real datasets
caps: 3D Gaussian splatting; closed loop; real data
desc: Photorealistic closed-loop simulator reconstructed from real driving logs with 360-degree rendering of inserted actors.

name: DriveArena
caps: generative simulation; world dreamer; traffic manager
desc: Closed-loop driving simulation where a generative world model renders the scene, so evaluation is not limited to reconstructed logged routes.

name: RoboDojo
verifier: Sim success checkers plus a standardized real evaluation station with scene reset
caps: unified sim+real leaderboard; remote real eval; generalist policies
desc: Unified leaderboard for generalist manipulation policies with a remotely accessible real-robot evaluation station, bridging sim scores and hardware results.

name: PhAIL
verifier: Time-to-success distributions and Human-Relative Throughput with bootstrap CIs
scale: Bin-to-bin picking, 4 object classes, Franka FR3
desc: Real-robot VLA leaderboard that reports throughput and time-to-success distributions anchored to human teleoperation on the same fixture, instead of binary success.

name: N-SCORE
verifier: Nonparametric sequential hypothesis test over arbitrary outcome metrics
scale: Protocol; up to 70% fewer trials than batch comparison
caps: evaluation protocol; sequential testing; non-binary outcomes
desc: A statistically rigorous sequential procedure for comparing policies on non-binary outcomes, cutting the number of real-robot trials needed for a decision.

name: PolaRiS
verifier: Sim success in neural-reconstructed scenes validated against paired real rollouts
desc: Scans real scenes into interactive simulation via neural reconstruction and reports higher sim-real correlation than prior sim benchmarks.

name: REALM
verifier: Sim success, validated on ~800 paired real/sim rollouts
caps: VLA generalization; perturbation factors; real-to-sim validation
desc: Generalization benchmark for VLAs whose perturbation factors are each validated against paired real rollouts, so the sim drop can be trusted.

name: Real-is-Sim
verifier: Success in a digital twin kept synchronized with the real scene
caps: digital twin; Embodied Gaussians; parallel evaluation
desc: Runs the policy inside a continuously synchronized digital twin of the real workspace, allowing parallel offline evaluation that tracks the real system.

name: RADAR
scale: Real-world physical dynamics and spatial reasoning tasks
caps: autonomous real eval; 3D metrics; sensor noise
desc: Real-world evaluation that scores outcomes by 3D IoU without a human in the loop, and quantifies how much sensor noise alone degrades that score.

name: AGENTSAFE
verifier: Multi-level diagnosis across perception, planning and execution
caps: hazardous instructions; AI2-THOR sandbox; diagnostic levels
desc: Hazardous-instruction suite for VLM embodied agents in an AI2-THOR sandbox, diagnosing whether the failure is in perception, planning or execution.

name: SafeVLA-Bench
verifier: Signal Temporal Logic invariants; safety rate, success-but-unsafe rate, violation severity
scale: 27 policy-benchmark entries on LIBERO and RoboCasa365
desc: Post-hoc safety audit of existing VLA benchmarks using temporal-logic invariants, finding high-success policies with a large fraction of unsafe episodes.

name: LIBERO-Safety
desc: Procedurally generated safety-critical variants of LIBERO tasks, exposing a trade-off between generalization and constraint satisfaction.

name: AttackVLA
verifier: Attack success rate in sim and on hardware
scale: Unified suite of existing adversarial and backdoor attacks
desc: Evaluation framework that runs existing adversarial and backdoor attacks against VLAs under one protocol in simulation and on real robots.

name: BeSafe-Bench
verifier: Rule-based and LLM-judge scoring of environment impact
desc: Behavioral safety benchmark spanning web, mobile and embodied VLM/VLA agents, scoring the consequences of executed actions rather than refusals.

name: SafeMindBench
caps: instruction risk; environment risk; plan ordering
desc: Multimodal safety questions covering risky instructions, risky environments, unsafe step ordering and requirement alignment for embodied planners.

name: ResponsibleRobotBench
scale: 23 multi-stage tasks across electrical, chemical and human hazards
desc: Multi-stage manipulation tasks with electrical, chemical and human hazards, reporting safe-success so completing the task unsafely does not count.

name: MuJoCo Playground
verifier: Environment suite, not a scored benchmark
scale: DM Control plus quadruped, humanoid and manipulation environments on MJX
desc: GPU-accelerated MuJoCo environment collection spanning control suites, legged and humanoid locomotion and manipulation, with sim-to-real recipes.

name: RoboMIND / RoboMIND 2.0
caps: multi-embodiment dataset; failure demonstrations; digital twin
desc: Large multi-embodiment manipulation dataset (RoboMIND, 2412.13877) extended to 310k trajectories with digital-twin simulation tasks for evaluation.

name: ManiSkill-HAB
desc: GPU-accelerated re-implementation of the Home Assistant Benchmark with low-level control, making whole-task mobile manipulation cheap to evaluate.

name: Isaac Lab-Arena
scale: Wraps LIBERO and RoboCasa; GPU-parallel policy evaluation
caps: composable scenes; policy evaluation; LeRobot integration
desc: Composable object, scene, embodiment and task layers for GPU-parallel policy evaluation that wraps existing suites such as LIBERO and RoboCasa.
